setup.pitch: Wintermere opened its presents before the village's traditional first gift reached the lonely house beyond the snow road. Now every gift is freezing shut again and the town hearths are going cold.
setup.gmSummary: Wintermere's Winterlight custom requires one 'First Gift' to be delivered beyond the giver's own household before anyone opens their own gifts. This year the First Gift—a chest of blankets, food, and medicine for the isolated Vale family—was quietly rerouted after the mountain road iced over. Festival master Hollis Vane ordered the hall opened anyway, planning to compensate the family later. The ritual's guardian, the Hearth Warden, interprets the broken sequence literally: gifts refreeze, hearths dim, and the abandoned gift sleigh becomes a moving icebound hazard. The party must uncover what happened, cross the snow road, recover or replace the First Gift, and decide whether Wintermere restores the old obligation, replaces it with a more reliable system, or ends the supernatural custom.
setup.background: Generations ago, Wintermere nearly lost an outer family during a blizzard because everyone assumed someone else had checked on them. Afterward the village adopted the First Gift rule: nobody opens a personal gift until one household has carried a practical gift to someone beyond its own walls. Over time, the tradition became cheerful pageantry. This year a real ice fall blocked the Vale road. Hollis Vane, under pressure to keep the celebration on schedule, stored the First Gift in the delivery barn and opened the gift hall anyway. The Vale family is alive but short on medicine and fuel. The Hearth Warden is not trying to punish generosity; it is enforcing the sequence the village asked it to guard.
setup.campaignFrame: Doctor Sera Moss sends the party from Hearthford with medicine intended for the isolated Vale household near Wintermere. The party returns to Hearthford after the last bell, and Sera remembers whether they treated the delivery as ceremony or actual care.

quest.objective: Find out why Winterlight failed, reach the Vale house, deliver or replace the First Gift, and resolve the Hearth Warden before the last bell.
quest.stakes: Wintermere's hearths are cooling, the Vale family is isolated without needed supplies, and panic may turn a broken tradition into a dangerous winter night.
quest.deadline: LAST WINTERLIGHT BELL: show four bell marks. Fill one after the gift hall, delivery barn, snow road, and Vale house. When the fourth fills, the Hearth Warden reaches the town square finale.
successConditions: The Vale household receives meaningful aid or an explicit alternate rescue.
The party resolves the Hearth Warden by completing, replacing, or ending the First Gift pact.
The truth about the rerouted delivery becomes known.
failureConditions: The party knowingly abandons the isolated household and the freezing town.
The gift hall is allowed to collapse into panic while all recovery routes are ignored.

facts.text: Wintermere's gifts are traditionally opened only after the First Gift reaches someone outside the giver's household.
The First Gift was stored in the delivery barn after the Vale road iced over instead of being delivered.
The Vale family is alive and needs medicine, fuel, and blankets more than ceremonial presents.
The Hearth Warden is enforcing the broken sequence rather than stealing gifts for itself.
The crisis can end by completing a meaningful First Gift, replacing the custom with a public winter-aid system, or breaking the supernatural pact.

locations.name: Wintermere Gift Hall
locations.description: A timber hall packed with reopened boxes, ribbons, evergreen garlands, and hearths whose flames are shrinking blue.

locations.name: Winterlight Delivery Barn
locations.description: A long stable with one ice-scarred sleigh, sealed gift chest, route boards, and snow rope hanging beside the east doors.

locations.name: Pine Cut Snow Road
locations.description: A narrow path between snow-heavy pines where broken sleigh runners, drifted trail markers, and a frozen creek offer safer passage than the ridge.

locations.name: Vale House
locations.description: A stone cottage beyond the fields with a low fire, nearly empty wood shed, and one window marked with the old Winterlight ribbon.

locations.name: Wintermere Bell Square
locations.description: The central square beneath a star-shaped bell frame, with gift tables, three public hearth braziers, and the last Winterlight bell overhead.

clues.revelation: Personal gifts are traditionally opened only after the First Gift reaches someone outside the giver's household.
sources: A carved beam in the gift hall reads FIRST CARRIED, THEN OPENED.
The delivery ledger records the First Gift departure time before the hall bell in every prior year.
The Vale hearth ribbon bears the same two-step symbol: walking boots before an open box.

clues.revelation: The First Gift was stored in the delivery barn and never reached the Vale house.
sources: The sealed chest remains in the barn with the Vale address tag intact.
Hollis's schedule marks HALL OPENED beside FIRST GIFT DELAYED.
Sleigh tracks leave the barn, turn back at the ice road, and return to the same bay.

A supply request from Lysa Vale is pinned to the delivery ledger.

scenes.title: Presents Freeze Shut
scenes.purpose: Launch the broken holiday sequence, establish the last-bell clock, and make the undelivered First Gift visible as the changed condition.
scenes.readAloud: The Winterlight hall is full of torn wrapping paper when the first scream goes up. Frost races backward across opened boxes. Toys, scarves, and books snap shut inside skins of blue ice. Around the room, hearth flames shrink to candle size. Hollis Vane stares at the bell schedule pinned to his sleeve and whispers, “The First Gift never made it.”
gmNotes: Show four LAST WINTERLIGHT BELL marks. Fill 1/4 when this scene ends.
No check is needed to learn that the First Gift was delayed; Hollis says it immediately once the crisis starts.
DC 12 Wisdom (Insight): success reveals Hollis personally made the decision to open the hall early; failure gives no false conclusion and his written schedule proves it later.
The carved beam FIRST CARRIED, THEN OPENED establishes the old sequence in physical evidence.
Send the party to the delivery barn before the crowd invents a supernatural thief.

scenes.title: The Gift Still Here
scenes.purpose: Prove the practical need, recover the delivery route, and offer a physical preparation choice.
scenes.readAloud: The delivery barn smells of horse sweat, pine tar, and cold iron. One sleigh sits crooked on a split runner. Beside it rests a large red chest whose tag reads VALE HOUSE — FIRST GIFT. The seal is unbroken. A route board on the wall shows the east road crossed out in charcoal, with a second line through the pine cut left untouched.
gmNotes: Fill LAST BELL 2/4 when the party leaves.
Opening the chest is allowed; the ritual is about delivery, not keeping wrapping pristine.
The manifest clearly lists medicine, blankets, lamp oil, and dried food.
DC 12 Intelligence (Investigation) on the route board finds Senna's pine-cut notes immediately. Failure costs a few minutes but the charcoal map nailed to the door still provides the route.
Taking snow rope and splitting supplies into backpacks gives advantage on the first snow-road hazard save; dragging the whole chest preserves ceremony but is harder.

runSteps.title: Give the alternate route

scenes.title: Snow That Moves Sideways
scenes.purpose: Make delivery itself a real obstacle and show the Warden protecting the route rather than hunting the party.
scenes.readAloud: Snow hangs heavy in the pines. Halfway through the cut, wind drives sideways across a frozen creek where an old footbridge has twisted off its stones. Beyond it, three lean wolves pace the bank—until a white-antlered figure steps silently between them and the trail to the Vale house. The wolves stop. The figure looks at what you are carrying.
gmNotes: Fill LAST BELL 3/4 when the party reaches the far side.

Frozen creek crossing: DC 12 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics). Success crosses safely; failure deals 1d6 cold/bludgeoning and drops one carried parcel 10 feet downslope, recoverable with an Action.
If the party took snow rope, the first failed crossing can be rerolled immediately.
Winter Wolves here are ordinary hungry wolves, not magical winter wolves. The Hearth Warden blocks them if the party is carrying aid toward the Vale house.
The party may fight the wolves, scare them off, or move while the Warden holds them. The Warden never attacks the party here.

runSteps.title: Make carrying matter

runSteps.title: Reveal the Warden's behavior
runSteps.text: It protects the Vale route from wolves.

runSteps.title: Keep multiple solutions
runSteps.text: Fight, scare off, or accept the Warden's protection.

exitChoices.label: Reach the Vale house
exitChoices.description: Finish the delivery the town skipped.

scenes.title: What the Gift Was For
scenes.purpose: Complete the rescue, establish that arrival matters more than wrapping, and give the party the material needed for all finale routes.
scenes.readAloud: The Vale house is warm only near the stove. Two children feed it twigs while an older woman lies under layered quilts, trying to repair a mitten. When she sees the medicine among your supplies, she laughs once and says, “Good. Put apologies by the door. Put that by the kettle.” Outside the window, white antlers pass between the pines.
gmNotes: Fill LAST BELL 4/4 when the party decides how the aid is delivered; the finale starts immediately afterward.
If the party brought the chest intact, opening it here completes the old First Gift act automatically.
If supplies were split or substituted, the act still counts if the Vales receive meaningful medicine, fuel, warmth, and food. Wrapping is irrelevant.
DC 12 Wisdom (Medicine) can stabilize Lysa's fever until morning. Failure does not make her die; the medicine still works over time, but she remains too weak to travel.
Lysa gives the Vale hearth ribbon, which shows the three lawful routes: carry, joined hands, shears.

runSteps.title: Deliver practical aid
runSteps.text: The ritual succeeds because someone arrives with help.

runSteps.text: Use her line that the custom is somebody arriving, not the box.

runSteps.title: Give the three-route symbol
runSteps.text: The hearth ribbon makes finale choices explicit before returning to town.

scenes.advanceWhen: The Vales have meaningful aid and the party returns toward Wintermere with the hearth ribbon and a chosen approach to the broken custom.

exitChoices.label: Return for the last bell
exitChoices.description: Take the completed delivery and its meaning back to Wintermere.

scenes.title: The Last Winterlight Bell
scenes.purpose: Resolve the tradition through delivery, public aid, or rejection of supernatural enforcement.
scenes.readAloud: The last Winterlight bell hangs above three public braziers whose flames are nearly blue. Frost crawls across every opened gift table. The white-antlered Hearth Warden walks into the square carrying a ribbon stiff with ice. It stops beneath the bell and says, “Gift carried. Hearth answered. Finish. Replace. Or break.”
gmNotes: The Hearth Warden starts at 52 HP.

FINISH route: if the Vales received meaningful aid, place the Vale hearth ribbon on the bell frame and complete 3 Hearth successes before 2 failures using DC 12 Charisma (Persuasion or Performance), Wisdom (Insight), or concrete acts reconnecting the delivered aid to the town. Each failure extinguishes one public brazier. At 2 failures this route closes but Replace and Break remain legal.

REPLACE route: create a public winter-aid compact at three stations—route board, supply reserve, household check roster. Each station is an Action and either automatic if the party already secured a concrete plan with Hollis/Senna/Lysa, or DC 12 Intelligence (Investigation), Wisdom (Survival), or Charisma (Persuasion). Three stations end the pact and preserve the Warden as a non-enforcing symbol.

BREAK route: the frozen ribbon-heart can be targeted after one successful hostile action or one brazier is deliberately extinguished. AC 13, 16 HP; destroying it drops the Warden to 0 HP and ends all supernatural Winterlight effects.
Direct combat to 0 HP is legal and has the same consequence as BREAK.

Initiative 20: Closing Hearth. One unattended brazier goes out. If all three are out, every creature in the square takes 1 cold damage at the start of its turn until a brazier is relit with an Action.

runSteps.title: State Finish, Replace, Break
runSteps.text: All three choices are legal and visible.

runSteps.title: Use braziers as pressure
runSteps.text: The clock changes the battlefield instead of hiding damage.

runSteps.title: Stop immediately when a route completes
runSteps.text: Do not force combat after the social objective resolves.

exitChoices.description: Keep the old tradition, now understood as a real welfare check.

scenes.title: Resolution: First Carried, Then Opened
scenes.purpose: Reward completing the tradition with clearer purpose.
scenes.readAloud: The Vale ribbon warms in your hands. Across Wintermere, frozen wrapping softens and hearth flames rise orange again. Nobody rushes to open a box. The hall waits while Senna hangs a new route board by the door.
gmNotes: Award 100 gp total and four Wintermere Favor tokens.
The First Gift remains, but it is rewritten as a mandatory welfare delivery rather than ceremonial pageantry.
Hollis publicly records the failure and future weather contingency.

runSteps.title: Rewrite the tradition
runSteps.text: Future First Gifts require an actual household check.

runSteps.title: Record reward
runSteps.text: Award 100 gp and Favor tokens.

scenes.advanceWhen: Rewards and the new written procedure are recorded.

scenes.title: Resolution: The Winter Roster
scenes.purpose: Reward replacing one symbolic delivery with a reliable system.
scenes.readAloud: Three boards go up before the bell stops ringing: routes, reserves, households. The Hearth Warden touches each one with two fingers. Its antlers shed their ice, becoming ordinary winter branches tied with red ribbon. The town's gifts thaw without anyone opening them yet.
gmNotes: Award 120 gp total and the Winter Roster token, a story item granting advantage on one future Wintermere check involving logistics, rescue, or public planning.
The supernatural enforcement ends, but the Warden remains as a harmless festival figure.
Senna becomes route captain if she accepts.

runSteps.title: Make the system concrete
runSteps.text: Routes, reserves, and check roster all need named owners.

runSteps.title: Reward structural repair
runSteps.text: Award 120 gp and the Winter Roster token.

scenes.advanceWhen: The three-part compact and rewards are recorded.

scenes.title: Resolution: Gifts Without a Warden
scenes.purpose: Respect rejecting supernatural enforcement while preserving the human obligation.
scenes.readAloud: The frozen ribbon-heart snaps. The Hearth Warden becomes a scatter of branches and old cloth at the foot of the bell. Every gift thaws. The three public braziers flare only after townsfolk begin carrying firewood and food toward the east road by hand.
gmNotes: Award 100 gp total.
Wintermere ends the supernatural First Gift pact.
The Vale rescue still matters; destroying the Warden does not retroactively fulfill material needs.

runSteps.title: Do not erase the rescue
runSteps.text: Aid to outer households remains a human responsibility.

runSteps.title: Record reward
runSteps.text: Award 100 gp.

scenes.advanceWhen: Rewards and the new nonmagical Winterlight practice are recorded.

encounters.name: Pine-Cut Wolves
encounters.summary: Three hungry wolves shadow the pine cut while the Hearth Warden blocks them from the Vale route.
encounters.resolution: Drive them off, fight, distract with food, or move past while the Warden holds the line.
encounters.talkOut: A DC 12 Wisdom (Animal Handling) check plus food drives the pack away; failure costs the food and they keep distance but remain present.
encounters.bypass: Move across the creek and continue while the Hearth Warden occupies the wolves.
encounters.objective: Carry the aid through the snow road without turning the Warden into an assumed enemy.

encounters.name: The Hearth Warden
encounters.summary: The guardian arrives at the last bell to force a decision about Wintermere's broken First Gift custom.
encounters.resolution: Complete Finish, complete Replace, destroy the ribbon-heart, or reduce the Warden to 0 HP.
encounters.talkOut: It accepts concrete proof of delivery or a three-part aid compact; ordinary persuasion without action is insufficient.
encounters.bypass: Finish and Replace are complete noncombat resolutions.
encounters.objective: Decide how Wintermere guarantees that isolated households are not forgotten again.

puzzles.prompt: Compare the crossed east road, sleigh damage, and old route notes to identify the pine-cut foot route.
puzzles.solution: The ridge road is unsafe for the sleigh, but the pine cut remains passable on foot with rope.
puzzles.bypass: DC 12 Investigation finds the usable route immediately.
puzzles.failForward: Senna's charcoal map remains nailed to the barn door even if the route-board check fails.

traps.trigger: Cross the twisted frozen-creek section without securing rope or choosing a careful path.
traps.effect: DC 12 Athletics or Acrobatics. Failure deals 1d6 cold/bludgeoning and drops one carried parcel 10 feet downslope.
traps.failForward: The parcel is recoverable with an Action; no required aid is destroyed.

items.name: Vale Hearth Ribbon
items.effect: Shows the three lawful Winterlight resolutions: delivery boots, joined hands, and shears.

items.name: Winter Roster Token

policies: Every required truth survives loss or hostility of any one NPC.
The First Gift remains practical aid even if the ceremonial chest is damaged or abandoned.
Failed road checks cost position, damage, or time but never destroy the only rescue route.

routes.trigger: Hollis is unavailable or refuses to cooperate.
routes.response: His schedule, the carved hall beam, and the sealed chest in the delivery barn prove the broken sequence.
stateChanges: The investigation begins without the festival master.

routes.response: Her charcoal pine-cut map is nailed to the barn door; split runner marks and snow rope still show why the sleigh turned back.

routes.trigger: The ceremonial First Gift chest is destroyed, lost, or left behind.
routes.response: Equivalent medicine, fuel, blankets, and food from Wintermere can fulfill the delivery if the party deliberately carries them to the Vales.
stateChanges: The ritual is about aid, not packaging.

routes.trigger: The party attacks the Hearth Warden on the road.
routes.response: It withdraws rather than counterattacking until the finale; wolf behavior, founder text, and Vale testimony still reveal its protective role.
stateChanges: The finale still offers Finish and Replace.

routes.trigger: The party skips or rushes earlier investigation and reaches the final scene without all resolution clues.
routes.response: The Warden states 'Finish. Replace. Or break.' and gestures to the Vale ribbon symbols before initiative.
stateChanges: Prepared play still provides easier noncombat completion.

pathPressure.principle: Preparation makes the snow route and noncombat finale safer, but the adventure remains finishable if rushed. The ending is never locked by skipped preparation; the party can still finish, but rushing carries the stated costs.
prepared: Snow rope allows a reroll on the first failed creek crossing.
Carrying real medicine/fuel/blankets makes the Vale delivery automatically meaningful.
A concrete aid plan established before returning makes Replace stations automatic.
rushed: Dragging the full chest is harder across the creek.
Skipping the route notes removes the snow-rope reroll.
Returning without a public aid plan requires checks at the three Replace stations.

cutOrder: If 25+ minutes behind, give the pine-cut route automatically in the barn.
If 15+ minutes behind on the snow road, reduce the wolves to two and let the Warden hold one at bay.
Never cut the Vale delivery, the Warden's true role, or the three final resolutions.
optionalOrder: Extended debate with Hollis in the hall.
Detailed barn inventory beyond practical aid.
Extra roleplay at the Vale house after medicine and fuel are delivered.

endings.name: First Carried, Then Opened
endings.condition: The party completes the Finish route.
endings.result: The First Gift survives as an explicit welfare delivery and Wintermere writes a weather contingency into the tradition.

endings.name: The Winter Roster
endings.condition: The party completes all three Replace stations.
endings.result: Wintermere replaces one ceremonial delivery with routes, reserves, and household checks; the Warden becomes harmless symbolism.

endings.name: Gifts Without a Warden
endings.condition: The Hearth Warden or ribbon-heart is destroyed.
endings.result: The supernatural pact ends; future outer-household aid becomes entirely a human responsibility.

checks.label: Complete one Hearth action
checks.success: One Hearth success is recorded and one public brazier flares brighter.
checks.failure: One public brazier goes out and one failure is recorded; at two failures Finish closes but Replace and Break remain legal.

encounters.objective: Carry practical aid through the pine cut.
encounters.start: Three hungry wolves stalk the far creek bank while the Hearth Warden blocks the route toward the Vale house.
encounters.bypass: Move past while the Warden holds them, or distract the pack with food.

creatures.name: Pine Wolf
creatures.trait: Hungry, Not Possessed: food or a successful DC 12 Animal Handling check can drive a wolf away.
creatures.tactics: Circle isolated carriers and retreat if badly hurt; they do not cross fire or pursue into the Vale yard.

encounters.end: The pack is driven off, bypassed, or the party reaches the far trail.

encounters.objective: Resolve Wintermere's broken First Gift obligation.
encounters.start: The Warden enters beneath the final bell as the public braziers dim.
encounters.bypass: Finish and Replace are complete noncombat victory routes.

creatures.name: Hearth Warden
creatures.trait: Frozen Ribbon-Heart: after one successful hostile action or one deliberately extinguished brazier, AC 13, 16 HP; destroying it reduces the Warden to 0 HP and ends the supernatural pact.
creatures.tactics: Pressure ritual actors, extinguish unattended braziers, and avoid chasing creatures who leave the square.

encounters.end: Finish succeeds, Replace completes, or the Warden reaches 0 HP.

hazards.failure: Take 1d6 cold/bludgeoning and drop one parcel 10 feet downslope.
hazards.failForward: Dropped aid remains recoverable; the route never disappears.

hazards.trigger: Initiative count 20 while the Warden remains unresolved.
hazards.failure: One unattended public brazier goes out.
hazards.success: If every brazier is attended or protected by a completed route action, no brazier goes out.
hazards.failForward: Even at zero braziers the other finale routes remain available.

rewards.when: The Finish ending resolves the crisis.
rewards.reward: 100 gp total and four Wintermere Favor tokens.

rewards.when: The Replace ending resolves the crisis.
rewards.reward: 120 gp total and the Winter Roster token.
100 gp total; future First Gift obligations are entirely nonmagical.

flowContract.principle: One winter rescue spine: diagnose the broken sequence, carry real aid, learn the guardian's purpose, and branch only at the final resolution.

continuity.relationshipEffect: Update Doctor Sera Moss's Hearthford relationship state based on how the party handled this night.
continuity.standaloneRule: The adventure still runs standalone; the Hearthford frame supplies continuity but is never required to solve the plot.
